title: 9/11 at 25: How the Global War on Terror Shaped a Generation
gist: A War on the Rocks members-only podcast episode marking 25 years since 9/11, in which Marine and Navy podcast hosts Matt Francis and Steve Walsh argue with host Nicole Wiley that the Global War on Terror expanded far beyond what operational success required.

insights.claim: The hosts of Marine Pulse and Sailor Pulse argue the Global War on Terror grew into something larger than was reasonable for operational success, framing over-expansion rather than execution as the central failure.
insights.so_what: A serving-officer consensus that the counter-terror mission was oversized supports continued defense budget rotation away from counter-terrorism toward great-power and homeland missions.
insights.quote: why the Global War on Terror grew into something larger than was reasonable for operational success
insights.speaker: War on the Rocks

insights.claim: The discussion frames post-9/11 policy as a case of emotion translating directly into action, implying that public grief, not cold operational analysis, set the scale of two decades of U.S. military commitment.
insights.so_what: A reusable lens for pricing future shock-driven policy: expect emotional national-security responses to overshoot their stated operational objective and to sustain spending beyond the threat.
insights.speaker: War on the Rocks

insights.claim: Twenty-five years after 9/11, a cohort of serving U.S. military personnel now describes the Global War on Terror primarily as a formative personal-career and institutional legacy rather than an ongoing campaign, signaling the conflict has passed into retrospective assessment.
insights.so_what: Watch for the institutional memory shift: forces that treat counter-terrorism as history reallocate training, procurement and doctrine attention toward peer conflict.
insights.locator: In this second episode of War on the Rocks' 9/11 at 25 series
insights.speaker: War on the Rocks

insights.claim: War on the Rocks is monetizing 9/11 retrospectives through a members-only premium podcast tier called Unspent Rounds, indicating defense-policy analysis is being pushed behind subscription paywalls rather than distributed free.
insights.so_what: Relevant to media and information-access models: primary national security commentary is increasingly gated, raising the cost of open-source defense intelligence.
insights.quote: A premium podcast hosted by War on the Rocks staff covering interesting topics with interesting people — for War on the Rocks members only.
insights.speaker: War on the Rocks
